title: The moving sea: tides
text:
If you visit a beach and come back six hours later, the sea may look very different. At one time, the water covers the sand. At another time, it has moved far away and left a wide, wet beach. This rising and falling of the sea is called the tide.

High tide and low tide

When the sea comes up the beach, it is high tide. When it moves back down, it is low tide. In most places, there are two high tides and two low tides every day. The time between one high tide and the next is about twelve hours.

What causes tides?

Tides are caused mainly by the Moon. The Moon pulls on the Earth with a force called gravity. The sea is made of water, which can move easily, so the Moon pulls the water towards it. The Sun pulls on the sea as well, but it is much further away, so its pull is weaker.

Living on the shore

Many animals live in the part of the beach between the high tide and low tide marks. Crabs hide in holes and snails close up their shells when the water goes out. At low tide, children can look for small creatures in rock pools.

Staying safe

Before going to the beach, it is a good idea to check a tide table. This is a chart that tells you when the tide will be high and low. People should never walk far out at low tide, because the sea can come back quickly.

Did you know?

Some places, such as the Bay of Fundy in Canada, have tides that are more than ten metres high.
